newsitem.title: CANADA: BCE slips on Bell Canada job cuts.
newsitem.headline: BCE slips on Bell Canada job cuts.

text.p: Shares of BCE Inc slipped 0.60 to 42.35 in heavy trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday after its Bell Canada unit announced further job cuts.
Bell Canada, Canada's largest telephone company, said in a letter sent to employees on Thursday that it planned to eliminate an additional 2,200 jobs over the next two to three months.
The cuts would be in addition to the 10,000 under a three-year restructuring plan ending this year, which would have reduced Bell Canada's workforce to 40,300.

In the letter, Bell Canada Chief Executive John McLennan said the utility's share of the C$8 billion Canadian long-distance telephone market had declined by 33 percent since 1992 when the federal government allowed competition in the sector.
McLennan said the market share loss included a two per cent decline in this year's first quarter.
"With the advent of local competition in 1998, we run a likely risk of even further decline in market share," McLennan said.

McLennan said about two-thirds of the latest job cuts would come from management, while the rest would be among administrative employees. Bell Canada plans to identify the affected workers toward the end of August.

McLennan said that despite the implementation of the three-year restructuring plan and other developments, Bell Canada's "comparatively high cost structure inhibits us from matching our rivals' prices for similar services."

Analyst Winfried Fruehauff of Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion Inc said BCE's stock price decline over Thursday and Friday might not be entirely related to the Bell Canada job cuts. Shares of BCE subsidiary Northern Telecom Ltd Nortel were off 3 to 141.25 on Friday.
